stories.title: FDA approves Tecentriq plus chemotherapy for stage III dMMR colon cancer
stories.takeaway: Atezolizumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy halved the hazard of recurrence or death in the ATOMIC trial.
stories.what_happened: On October 8 FDA approved atezolizumab with fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin chemotherapy for resected stage III mismatch-repair-deficient colon cancer. ATOMIC randomized 712 patients; disease-free-survival HR was 0.50 (95% CI 0.35–0.73), with 36-month DFS of 86% versus 76%.
stories.why_it_matters: For CRC organ chips, this underscores the need for biomarker-stratified tissue and immune components to model immunotherapy; epithelial viability alone cannot predict PD-L1 blockade response.
stories.caveat: The trial was open-label, severe adverse events increased, and an overall-survival advantage remains unproven.

stories.title: TRexBio prices $116.7M IPO for tissue-resident Treg immunology
stories.takeaway: An earlier IPO plan became a priced $14-per-share offering on October 9, a substantive financing milestone.
stories.what_happened: TRexBio priced 8,333,334 shares at $14 for roughly $116.7M gross proceeds, with trading expected under TRXB and closing expected October 13.
stories.why_it_matters: Tissue-resident regulatory T cells matter for intestinal immune tolerance; the financing also shows how translational immunology programs can access public capital.
stories.caveat: The offering is not yet closed, and financing does not validate clinical efficacy or prove tissue-specific immune modulation.

stories.title: Viatris agrees to acquire Pacira for $1.65B
stories.takeaway: Commercial non-opioid pain drugs and infrastructure command a premium compared with early-stage platform promises.
stories.what_happened: Viatris announced an all-cash $36.50-per-share deal to buy Pacira, adding marketed Exparel and Zilretta; closing is expected by year-end.
stories.why_it_matters: A commercialization lesson for MPS: validated outputs, scalable operations and customer-ready infrastructure can matter as much as device novelty.
stories.caveat: The acquisition has not closed, and a revenue-generating drug business is not directly comparable to a precommercial chip platform.

stories.title: Four flavonoids show different microbiome and epithelial-barrier effects in colitis
stories.takeaway: Quercetin, kaempferol, luteolin and apigenin were not interchangeable in a new mouse colitis study.
stories.what_happened: An October 9 npj Science of Food paper found compound-specific effects: quercetin reduced FITC-dextran permeability, apigenin and luteolin increased tight-junction proteins, and kaempferol most strongly restored microbiome diversity.
stories.why_it_matters: A gut chip could separate direct epithelial barrier/ROS protection from microbiota-mediated benefits by testing these interventions with and without microbes.
stories.caveat: Mouse associations between gut, brain and microbiome outcomes are not proof of causal mediation or clinical IBD efficacy.

stories.title: Synbiotic yeast cell wall and H. coagulans increases butyrate in vitro
stories.takeaway: The combination produced more butyrate than either component in 48-hour fecal fermentation.
stories.what_happened: An October 9 Scientific Reports study compared yeast cell wall, Heyndrickxia coagulans SANK70258, their combination and control in healthy-donor fecal cultures. The combined treatment had the highest butyrate concentration.
stories.why_it_matters: In CD/FMT chip work, microbial metabolic output could be a more mechanistic readout than taxonomic composition; a chip can test whether extra butyrate actually protects epithelium.
stories.caveat: Healthy-donor short-term fermentation has no intestinal epithelium, does not establish cross-feeding causality, and is not evidence of clinical benefit.
